summary: Hamburg presented plans in August 2020 to make the Jungfernstieg largely car-free from October 2020, and in November 2023 the Senate adopted a goal of 80 percent of trips by walking, cycling and public transport by 2030. In 2026 the city raised on-street parking fees for the first time since 2022 and began a pilot of licence-plate-based digital parking control. Westfield Hamburg-Überseequartier opened in April 2025 with a ticketless, dynamically priced car park, a city-centre car park at Gröninger Hof is planned to become housing, and Hamburg counted 5,063 public charging points in April 2026, including new points in APCOA and MediaMarkt car parks.

items.text: Hamburg presented plans in August 2020 to make the Jungfernstieg largely car-free from October 2020, leaving it to public transport, deliveries and cyclists, with a fuller reconstruction to follow from autumn 2021.
items.source_title: Plans to make Jungfernstieg free of cars presented

items.text: In a February 2020 answer to a parliamentary question, the Senate said the P+R annual card price was cut from 200 to 100 euros on 1 January 2019, and that by the end of 2019 the P+R operating company had taken over almost all district P+R sites and introduced paid parking almost everywhere, with live free-space display.
items.source_title: Drucksache 21/20019: Unsinnige rot-grüne Umbau- und Gebührenabsichten für Park+Ride am U-Bahnhof Ohlstedt – Wann werden die Planungen endlich vorgelegt?

items.text: The Senate adopted a mobility transition strategy aiming for 80 percent of trips to be made by walking, cycling and public transport by 2030, with expanding public transport through the Hamburg-Takt as its first field of action.

The transport authority announced the first on-street parking fee rise since 2022: the city-centre zone goes from 3.50 to 4.00 euros per hour, the other zones also rise by 50 cents, and the resident permit rises from 65 to 70 euros when applied for online. Meters were to switch to the new fees step by step over the following weeks, and private electric cars keep free parking at meters.
items.source_title: Faire Gebührenanpassung beim Parken im Rahmen der Inflationsentwicklung

items.text: A city page on electric mobility says cars with an E plate may park free at all parking meters up to the maximum time, but that under current law this exemption is set to end on 31 December 2026.

A pilot started in ten neighbourhood parking areas in Harvestehude and Borgfelde/Hohenfelde/Uhlenhorst. Drivers enter their licence plate at the meter or in an app instead of displaying a paper ticket or permit, and a camera-equipped scan car checks plates against stored parking rights.
items.source_title: Pilotprojekt zur Digitalisierung des Parkraummanagements startet ab 7. Juli in zwei Quartiersparkgebieten

items.text: The city extended its 'Feierabendparken' scheme in a pilot to three REWE and PENNY supermarket car parks, which residents and visitors can book digitally overnight and on Sundays for 3 euros per night. The city says Hamburg is the first city in Germany to include these chains.
items.source_title: Feierabendparken in Hamburg: Angebot wird auf REWE und PENNY ausgeweitet

items.text: Westfield Hamburg-Überseequartier in HafenCity opened on 8 April 2025, a mixed-use quarter with about 170 shops, restaurants and leisure venues, a cinema, hotels and flats.
items.source_title: Überseequartier Hamburg: So sieht es im neuen HafenCity-Shoppingzentrum aus

items.text: Westfield's own undated parking page lists about 2,500 car spaces open 24 hours, dynamic pricing with a daily maximum of 39 euros, and a free first hour for members of its Westfield Club.

According to its equipment supplier, the Westfield Hamburg-Überseequartier car park went live in 2025 with ticketless entry using 34 licence-plate-recognition cameras, dynamic pricing, camera-based space guidance and mobile payment.
items.source_title: Westfield Hamburg-Überseequartier – A tailored parking solution for one of Europe's largest inner-city projects (Designa reference)

items.text: The city announced that a car park at Neue Gröningerstraße 12 in the Altstadt (Gröninger Hof) is to become a cooperative housing scheme with 90 subsidised flats. Preparatory work was to start in May 2025 and demolition and conversion in summer 2025.

After the KaDeWe Group filed for insolvency in January 2024, its three department stores, including the Alsterhaus in Hamburg, moved to a new operating company under the Thai Central Group and continued trading without a break.

E.ON opened 18 public fast-charging points (50 and 150 kW) on the seventh deck of the car park at the new MediaMarkt flagship at Mönckebergstraße 1. They are open to all drivers during the car park's opening hours.
items.source_title: E.ON eröffnet Ladepark an MediaMarkt-Filiale in Hamburg

items.text: APCOA reported that Hamburg was the focus of its 2025 charging roll-out, with 55 charging points activated at its Hanseviertel, Gänsemarkt, Elbphilharmonie and Blankenese P1/P2 sites.
items.source_title: Apcoa realisierte 2025 gut 300 Ladepunkte in seinen Parkhäusern

items.text: Hamburg counted 5,063 public charging points on 1 April 2026, about 40 percent more than a year earlier. The growth was helped by a concession model in use since 2025, under which several private operators each build 500 public charging points.
items.source_title: Hamburg zählt mehr als 5.000 öffentliche Ladepunkte

items.text: According to preliminary figures cited by a transport authority spokesperson, the HVV expected more than 1.1 billion journeys in 2024, a record, compared with 1.096 billion in 2019. About 2.7 million passengers travelled on an average weekday, around 6 percent more than in the previous timetable year.
items.source_title: Hamburg, Nürnberg, Berlin: Boom beim Nahverkehr

items.text: The economics authority projected about 16.1 million overnight stays in 2024, 1.1 percent more than in 2023, and reported a record 1.3 million cruise passengers and hotel room occupancy of 77 percent.
